question: A car moving with an initial velocity of $4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ accelerates uniformly at $3\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ for $3\ \text{s}$. Find its final velocity.

question: A vehicle covers a distance at $30\ \text{km h}^{-1}$ and returns the same distance at $90\ \text{km h}^{-1}$. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
anchor: For equal distances the average speed is $\dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}$ (total distance over total time).
why: For equal distances the average speed is $\dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}$ (total distance over total time). $v_{av} = \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2} = \dfrac{2\times 30\times 90}{30+90}$ $v_{av} = 45\ \text{km h}^{-1}$

why: For equal distances the average speed is $\dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}$ (total distance over total time). $v_{av} = \dfrac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2} = \dfrac{2\times 60\times 30}{60+30}$ $v_{av} = 40\ \text{km h}^{-1}$

question: A projectile is launched with a speed of $40\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ above the horizontal on level ground. Find its horizontal range. (Take $g = 9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.)
anchor: The horizontal range of a projectile on level ground is $R = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g}$.
why: The horizontal range of a projectile on level ground is $R = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g}$. $R = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g} = \dfrac{40^{2}\sin(2\times45^{\circ})}{9.8}$ $R = 163\ \text{m}$

question: A body of mass $7\ \text{kg}$ moves in a circle of radius $6\ \text{m}$ with a uniform speed of $16\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Find the centripetal force.
anchor: The centripetal force on a body of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ in a circle of radius $r$ is $F = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$.
why: The centripetal force on a body of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ in a circle of radius $r$ is $F = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$. $F = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} = \dfrac{7\times16^{2}}{6}$ $F = 299\ \text{N}$

why: Stress is the restoring force per unit area, $\sigma = \dfrac{F}{A}$. $\sigma = \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{8000}{14\times10^{-4}}\ \text{Pa}$ $\sigma = 5.71\ \text{MPa}$

question: A steel bar under a stress of $400\ \text{MPa}$ shows a strain of $0.001$. Find Young's modulus.

question: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of $200\ \text{g}$ of water by $20\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$? (Specific heat capacity of water $= 4.2\ \text{J g}^{-1}\,^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$.)

why: Linear expansion is $\Delta L = L\alpha\,\Delta T$. $\Delta L = L\alpha\Delta T = 1\times 17\times10^{-6}\times 80\ \text{m}$ $\Delta L = 1.36\ \text{mm}$

why: Charles' law states that at constant pressure $\dfrac{V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{V_2}{T_2}$ (T in kelvin). $V_2 = V_1\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 8\times\dfrac{350}{300}$ $V_2 = 9.33\ \text{L}$

question: An object is placed $50\ \text{cm}$ from a concave mirror of focal length $5\ \text{cm}$. Find the distance of the real image from the mirror.
anchor: The mirror formula (real-is-positive convention) is $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{v}$.
why: The mirror formula (real-is-positive convention) is $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{v}$. $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{50}$ $v = 5.56\ \text{cm}$

question: A ray of light incident at $60^{\circ}$ in air is refracted at $20^{\circ}$ in a medium. Find the refractive index of the medium.
anchor: Snell's law gives the refractive index as $n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$.
why: Snell's law gives the refractive index as $n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$. $n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \dfrac{\sin 60^{\circ}}{\sin 20^{\circ}}$ $n = 2.53$

why: The lens formula (Cartesian sign convention) is $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$. $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{50}$ $v = 21.4\ \text{cm}$

question: Find the power of a convex lens of focal length $50\ \text{cm}$.
anchor: Power of a lens is $P = \dfrac{1}{f}$ with $f$ in metres (dioptre).

question: Two point charges of $9\ \mu\text{C}$ and $8\ \mu\text{C}$ are placed $5\ \text{m}$ apart in air. Find the force between them. (Take $k = 9\times10^{9}\ \text{N m}^{2}\text{C}^{-2}$.)
anchor: Coulomb's law gives the force between two point charges, $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^{2}}$.
why: Coulomb's law gives the force between two point charges, $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^{2}}$. $F = \dfrac{k q_1 q_2}{r^{2}} = \dfrac{9\times10^{9}\times9\times10^{-6}\times8\times10^{-6}}{5^{2}}$ $F = 0.0259\ \text{N}$

question: A capacitor of capacitance $18\ \mu\text{F}$ is charged to a potential difference of $60\ \text{V}$. Calculate the energy stored in it.

question: A radioactive sample initially has $1600$ nuclei and a half-life of $5\ \text{days}$. How many nuclei remain undecayed after $15\ \text{days}$?
anchor: After $n$ half-lives, $N = \dfrac{N_0}{2^{n}}$ with $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}}$.
why: After $n$ half-lives, $N = \dfrac{N_0}{2^{n}}$ with $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}}$. $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \dfrac{15}{5} = 3$ $N = \dfrac{N_0}{2^{n}} = \dfrac{1600}{2^{3}} = 200$

question: A radioactive sample initially has $320$ nuclei and a half-life of $5\ \text{days}$. How many nuclei remain undecayed after $15\ \text{days}$?
